cards.explanation: The answer is Christ. Paul says that at that time the Gentiles were separate from Christ, and that's the first thing on his list. Friends, I know a little about being left on the outside, but this is a whole other level.
The answer is False. Paul says the Gentiles were "…without hope and without God in the world." That's a heavy thing to read. Hold onto this one, friends. You're about to see what comes next.

The answer is True. Paul says, "But now in Christ Jesus you who once were far away have been brought near through the blood of Christ." Far away, then brought near. Same people, brand new spot. And I'll say it again, friends, because I love it: BROUGHT NEAR.

The answer is hostility. Paul says Christ tore down "…the dividing wall of hostility". Think about that, friends. Hostility is the kind of wall you can't knock through with a rolling pin, and He took it down anyway.

The answer is that He abolished the law of commandments. Paul says Christ tore down the wall "…by abolishing in His flesh the law of commandments and decrees." He did it in His flesh. That's the line, friends, and it's a big one.

The answer is one new man. Paul says Christ did it "…to create in Himself one new man out of the two, thus making peace". Two groups went in and one new man came out. It's not a mixed batch, friends. It's a brand new one, and it's made in Him.

The answer is the cross. Paul says Christ reconciled both groups "…to God in one body through the cross…" One body, one cross, both groups. I'll tell you, friends, this is the heart of the whole stop.
The answer is those far away and those near. Paul says Christ preached "…peace to you who were far away and peace to those who were near." He didn't pick a side of the room. Peace went to both.
The answer is True. Paul says, "For through Him we both have access to the Father by one Spirit." Notice the word both. Same Christ, same Spirit, same Father. Nobody needs a second door.

The answers are citizens and household. Paul says they are "…no longer strangers and foreigners…" and that they are "…fellow citizens with the saints and members of God’s household…" Strangers and foreigners got a new standing, friends. They're citizens now, right alongside the saints. And household is a family word, not a visitor word.

The answer is Christ Jesus Himself. Paul says the building is built "…on the foundation of the apostles and prophets, with Christ Jesus Himself as the cornerstone." The apostles and prophets are in the foundation, but Christ Jesus is the cornerstone. And that's a spot nobody else gets.

The answer is temple. Paul says that in Christ the whole building is fitted together and grows into "…a holy temple in the Lord." And I'll tell you, friends, a good fit matters. Even a cookie box won't close if the pieces don't line up.

The answer is False. Paul says, "…in Him you too are being built together into a dwelling place for God in His Spirit." The words "you too" matter here, friends. The Gentiles are in the building, and nobody stands outside it.
